final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Answer.**
Yes. 2 FloodNet community sensors within 600 m have logged 14 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years, the most recent starting 2026-09-01 05:39 UTC [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 815 mm (32.1 in) on 2026-05-20 [floodnet]. 1 sensor that logged events is flagged by FloodNet for maintenance, so its depths are not used for the peak [floodnet]. The highest depth a flagged sensor recorded was 1172 mm (46.1 in) on 2026-05-20 [floodnet]. USGS surveyed 2 Hurricane Ida high-water marks within 800 m of this address; the highest stood 0.76 ft above ground; the highest water surface elevation was 48.2 ft NAVD88 [ida_hwm]. Nearest mark: Intersection of 182nd St. and 90th Ave., Jamaica, Queens (174 m away) [ida_hwm]. 89 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 48 sewer backup, 28 catch basin, 10 street flooding, 3 manhole overflow [nyc311].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.

Checks run: citations and numbers on every claim; lead rules on the answer, which is the cited text word for word.
